title: Multiple dispatch and method specificity
outcome: Design generic operations over owned types and resolve overlapping method signatures explicitly.

exercises.title: Add a zero-size shape
exercises.hint: Check the boundary without rejecting a valid degenerate shape.
exercises.answer: The constructor permits nonnegative dimensions, including zero.

exercises.title: Reject an invalid dimension
exercises.hint: Dispatch does not replace domain validation.
exercises.answer: A method for the right type can still receive scientifically invalid values unless its contract prevents them.

exercises.title: Trace both arguments
exercises.task: Call classify with an integer in each position separately.
exercises.expected: Different methods handle the two cases.
exercises.hint: Method selection uses the positional type tuple.
exercises.answer: There is no requirement that one argument be a special receiver.

exercises.title: Resolve the overlap
exercises.expected: The explicit intersection method is selected.
exercises.hint: Neither one-sided signature alone expresses the complete overlap rule.
exercises.answer: An intersection method documents behavior and prevents ambiguity.

exercises.title: Keep an unsupported case visible
exercises.task: Pass two floating-point values to classify.
exercises.answer: A catch-all fallback should be added only when its semantics are defined.

exercises.title: Extend an owned interface
exercises.task: Sketch another Shape subtype and an area method.
exercises.expected: The generic total can use the operation if its laws hold.
exercises.hint: An abstract type does not implement the behavior itself.
exercises.answer: Test the new method and invariants rather than assuming subtype membership proves interface correctness.
